- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates; apply upward bias correction, particularly in early forecast horizon.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment spikes to 1.0, leading to exaggerated overshoots in 3–7 day horizon; dampen forecast peaks.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–30 day horizon — if forecast is >20% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 15–30% unless sentiment confirms bullish trend.
- Model underestimates long-term (30+ day) outcomes when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — increase forecast by 10–25% if sentiment is ≤ 0.3 over last 5 days.
- Forecast horizon 1–7 days: model often misses sentiment-driven volatility — adjust for sentiment momentum (e.g., if sentiment rises >0.5, add 5–10% to forecast).
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.33” values, model tends to underperform — increase forecast by 5–15% for 30-day horizon if sentiment is flat or negative.
